title: Frozen Coffee Drink, Decaffeinated, with Non-Dairy Milk and Whipped Cream

content.title: About
content.content: The frozen coffee drink, decaffeinated, with non-dairy milk and whipped cream is a refreshing beverage made from ground coffee that has undergone decaffeination, blended with a light plant‑based milk (such as oat or almond) and topped with a airy, dairy‑free whipped topping. Served as a frozen frothy treat similar to a frappe, it is suitable for those avoiding caffeine and dairy.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Decaffeination retains most of the original coffee flavor while removing almost all caffeine.
Plant milks like oat, almond or soy give the drink a smooth texture and a subtle natural sweetness.
Vegan whipped cream is often made from coconut cream or other plant‑based creams, making it suitable for vegans.
Frozen coffee beverages are a staple of summer menus worldwide, especially in hot climates.
Sugar levels can be adjusted—from completely unsweetened to a sweetened version according to taste.

items.title: Low caffeine content
items.content: Decaffeinated coffee provides the aroma and taste without the stimulating effect of caffeine, which is ideal for caffeine‑sensitive individuals.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Coffee contains polyphenols that help combat free radicals and support cardiovascular health.

items.title: Source of plant protein and vitamins
items.content: Non‑dairy milk adds a modest amount of protein, B‑vitamins, and calcium, especially when fortified.

items.title: Supports digestion
items.content: Certain plant milks (e.g., oat) contain soluble fiber that can aid normal digestion.

items.title: Low‑calorie dessert option
items.content: When made with limited sweetener and without heavy cream, the drink can be a light treat with moderate calories.

items.title: Allergy to plant ingredients
items.content: Some people may be allergic to nuts, soy, or oats used in the plant milk.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Sweetened versions may contain significant sugar, which is undesirable for diabetics or those watching weight.

items.title: Coffee acidity
items.content: Even without caffeine, coffee remains acidic and may irritate the stomach of people with gastritis or ulcers.

items.title: Food additives
items.content: Commercial products may contain stabilizers and emulsifiers that are not suitable for all consumers.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the frozen coffee in a glass or cup, garnish with an extra swirl of dairy‑free whipped topping, and optionally dust with cinnamon or cocoa powder. Add a splash of flavored syrup (vanilla, caramel, etc.) for extra sweetness if desired.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the prepared drink in the freezer at –18 °C (0 °F) or lower. For longer storage (over two weeks) sugar may crystallize, so it is best consumed within a week.
